name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
description: Ireland’s archaeology museum on Kildare Street, with prehistoric gold, Viking finds and bog bodies.

name: Trinity College
places: Book of Kells, Old Library, Trinity College
description: Ireland’s oldest university, founded in 1592. Its Old Library holds the Book of Kells, a medieval illuminated gospel book.

name: The Spire
description: A 120-metre stainless-steel needle in the middle of O’Connell Street, put up in 2003 where Nelson’s Pillar once stood.

name: General Post Office
description: Dublin’s main post office, headquarters of the rebels in the 1916 Easter Rising. A museum inside tells the story.

name: 14 Henrietta Street
description: A Georgian townhouse museum showing its life as a grand home and later as a crowded tenement, through to the 1970s.

name: The Cobblestone
description: A pub in Smithfield known for its nightly traditional Irish music sessions.

name: St Stephen’s Green
description: A Victorian park in a Georgian square at the top of Grafton Street, with a lake, bridges and statues.

name: Dublin Castle
description: The former seat of British rule in Ireland, with state apartments, courtyards, and the Chester Beatty museum of manuscripts in its grounds.
